**Estado atual (verificado)**
- A Fase 1 de 8W2N (V7C2) está mesclada ao `main`; este worktree está no mesmo commit. Os oito protótipos estáticos e o design system estão prontos.

- **O sistema ASDF ainda não tem nenhum componente de aplicação web.** As dependências de servidor do ADR D2K9 (Clack, Hunchentoot, Ningle, Spinneret) ainda não estão no `qlfile`. Tudo das Fases 2 a 7 é trabalho novo.

**Natureza da tarefa-pai.** 8W2N é ampla e composta; o próprio plano exige decomposição em sub-tarefas atômicas no início da sessão. As Fases 2 a 7 constroem duas aplicações server-side segregadas. Proponho a seguinte decomposição em sub-tarefas, cada uma um incremento coerente e verificável:

1. **Fundação e sessão** (Fases 2-3): esqueleto Clack/Hunchentoot, roteamento Ningle, renderização Spinneret, HTMX como ativo estático sob CSP estrita, layout base a partir dos tokens, login por seleção sem senha, sessão de servidor e segregação das duas aplicações por papel. Entrega dois servidores que sobem, servem o layout tematizado e estabelecem sessão.
2. **Serviços de ciclo** (Fase 4): laços de ranqueamento, decaimento e expiração, persistindo `opportunity_scores` a partir do motor de scoring, no ciclo acelerado da concepção.
3. **Aplicação do agente** (Fase 5 + responsividade).
4. **Aplicação do gerente** (Fase 6 + responsividade).

**Declaração de entendimento (recorte recomendado para esta sessão — sub-tarefa 1).** O objetivo é erguer a fundação executável das duas aplicações web server-side (servidor, roteamento, renderização, layout base do design system) e a identificação por seleção com sessão e segregação por papel, sem ainda implementar as listas de oportunidades nem os serviços de ciclo. A abordagem segue estritamente o stack do ADR D2K9, adicionando as dependências ao `qlfile`/`qlfile.lock` via qlot e materializando o layout a partir dos protótipos da V7C2. O critério de pronto: ambos os servidores sobem sem avisos de compilação, servem o layout base tematizado e responsivo sob CSP estrita, o login por seleção estabelece a sessão correta para cada papel, e a verificação aplicável (compilação limpa, Parachute, mallet, HTML/CSS) passa.

# Descrição (o que será feito)

Erguer a fundacao executavel das duas aplicacoes web server-side segregadas do LeadScorer, a do
agente e a do gerente, conforme as Fases 2 e 3 do plano da tarefa-pai 8W2N. Compreende o esqueleto
Clack sobre Hunchentoot, o roteamento com Ningle, a renderizacao com Spinneret, o HTMX 2.0.x
servido como ativo estatico sob CSP estrita com 'htmx.config.allowEval' em falso, o layout base
derivado dos tokens do design system e dos protótipos da V7C2, e a identificacao por selecao do
usuario semeado, sem senha, com sessao de servidor e segregacao das duas aplicacoes por papel.
Nao contempla as listas de oportunidades, o painel de indicadores nem os servicos de ciclo, que
sao objeto das sub-tarefas seguintes de 8W2N.


# Motivações (por que será feito)

8W2N e ampla e composta e o seu plano exige decomposicao em sub-tarefas atomicas no inicio da
sessao. A Fase 1 (V7C2) entregou os protótipos estaticos e o modelo economico (W8H5); a
persistencia (9P4D) esta pronta. A fundacao executavel e a sessao sao a precondicao comum das
aplicacoes do agente e do gerente: sem servidor, layout base e identificacao com segregacao por
papel, nenhuma das telas subsequentes pode ser servida. Esta sub-tarefa isola esse nucleo comum
em um incremento coerente e verificavel, evitando acoplar a sua validacao a das telas de negocio.


# Recursos e dados necessários

- Stack de aplicacao do ADR D2K9 (Clack, Hunchentoot, Ningle, Spinneret, Postmodern, HTMX
  2.0.x), a ser fixada no 'qlfile' e no 'qlfile.lock' via qlot;
- Protótipos estaticos da V7C2 em '.claude/assets/examples/' como referencia do layout base
  (navbar, wordmark, menu responsivo, tema escuro Gray 100);
- Tokens do design system em '.claude/assets/tokens/' e as regras de '.claude/rules/design.md';
- Fontes IBM Plex locais em '.claude/assets/fonts/';
- Schema e seed da persistencia (9P4D): tabelas 'sales_agents', 'sales_managers' e demais, para
  a lista de selecao do login;
- Concepcao funcional em 'docs/concepcao-inicial.md' (estorias de identificacao e acesso,
  arquitetura server-side, segregacao das aplicacoes).


# Plano de trabalho (como será feito)

O plano detalhado e desenvolvido no modo de planejamento da sessao e registrado no worklog. Em
linhas gerais, seguindo as Fases 2 e 3 da tarefa-pai:

1. Fixar as dependencias de aplicacao no 'qlfile'/'qlfile.lock' via qlot e adicionar os
   componentes de aplicacao ao sistema ASDF;
2. Montar o esqueleto Clack sobre Hunchentoot, o roteamento Ningle e a renderizacao Spinneret,
   com o layout base a partir dos tokens e a servir o HTMX como ativo estatico sob CSP estrita;
3. Implementar a identificacao por selecao do usuario semeado, sem senha, com sessao de servidor
   e a segregacao das duas aplicacoes por papel;
4. Validar a responsividade do layout base (iPhone 13), a conformidade com o design system e a
   verificacao de software aplicavel.


# Riscos e ressalvas

- O padrao de integracao HTMX com Common Lisp nao e coberto por documentacao oficial e e
  implementado manualmente por inspecao do cabecalho HX-Request (ADR D2K9); nesta fase o HTMX e
  apenas provisionado como ativo, sem fragmentos de negocio;
- A adicao das dependencias de servidor ao 'qlfile' altera o grafo de dependencias e pode
  reintroduzir avisos de redefinicao analogos ao caso do UIOP/Postmodern ja tratado no
  'leadscorer.asd'; a compilacao limpa deve ser verificada apos a fixacao;
- A segregacao por papel sem gestao de papeis exige duas aplicacoes distintas; a decisao de como
  materializar a segregacao (dois handlers, duas portas ou um discriminador de sessao) deve ser
  fixada no planejamento.


# Dependências

- blocks:
- blocked-by: 9P4D, V7C2


# Definição de pronto

- As duas aplicacoes, do agente e do gerente, sobem sem avisos de compilacao e servem o layout
  base tematizado (tema escuro Gray 100, IBM Plex local) em conformidade com o design system;
- O HTMX 2.0.x e servido como ativo estatico sob CSP estrita com 'htmx.config.allowEval' em
  falso;
- O login por selecao do usuario semeado, sem senha, estabelece a sessao de servidor correta
  para cada papel, e as duas aplicacoes ficam segregadas;
- O layout base e responsivo no iPhone 13;
- A verificacao de software aplicavel passa (compilacao e carga sem avisos, testes Parachute,
  linter mallet, e as verificacoes de HTML, CSS e YAML pertinentes).

- Agents: `seed-sales-agents` (`seed.lisp:123-136`) inserts `INSERT INTO sales_agents (name, username, sales_manager_id) VALUES ($1,$2,$3) RETURNING id`, passing `(derive-username agent)`.
- `regional_offices` gets no username (`seed-regional-offices`, `seed.lisp:96-106`, inserts name only).
- Source is `data/normalized/sales_teams.csv` (columns `regional_office`, `manager`, `sales_agent`), read by `read-normalized-csv` (`seed.lisp:87`). Data dir: `*data-directory*` = system-relative `data/normalized/` (`seed.lisp:13`).
- Orchestrator `(seed-database)` (`seed.lisp:324-352`, exported): assumes active connection; in one transaction `TRUNCATE ... RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE` then seeds offices → managers → agents → accounts → products → justifications → opportunities → engagements. Idempotent, returns T. Canonical counts to expect: `sales_agents`=35, `sales_managers`=6, `regional_offices`=3 (`verify.lisp:11-19`).

## 6. ASDF system structure — `leadscorer.asd`

- Immutable-system registration: `(asdf:register-immutable-system "uiop")` at top of file (`leadscorer.asd:8`), evaluated at read time BEFORE dependencies load. Rationale (`:3-7`): UIOP ships inside the SBCL image; registering it immutable prevents Postmodern's dependency graph from reloading the Quicklisp UIOP over the built-in one (which would emit hundreds of redefinition warnings). Ref: worklog task 9P4D.
- System `"leadscorer"` (`:10-26`):
  - `:depends-on ("fare-csv" "postmodern")`
  - `:serial t`
  - Components — module `"src"` with files in order: `package`, `csv`, `model`, `scoring`, `validation`, `db`, `migrate`, `seed`, `verify`. (Note: `csv` and `validation` files are compiled though not in the read list; `csv.lisp` defines the exported CSV API, `validation.lisp` defines `run-validation`/`aggregation-comparison`.)
  - `:in-order-to ((asdf:test-op (asdf:test-op "leadscorer/tests")))`
- Test system `"leadscorer/tests"` (`:28-43`):
  - `:depends-on ("leadscorer" "parachute")`, `:serial t`
  - Module `"tests"`: `main`, `scoring`, `validation`, `persistence`
  - `:perform (test-op ...)` runs `parachute:test :leadscorer/tests`, errors unless status `:passed`.
- Dependency pinning via qlot: `qlfile` lists `fare-csv`, `parachute`, `postmodern`; `qlfile.lock` pins Quicklisp dist `2026-01-01` (postmodern/parachute `ql-2026-01-01`, fare-csv `ql-2024-10-12`).
- DB setup entry point `scripts/db-setup.lisp`: `(require :asdf)` → `(asdf:load-system :leadscorer)` → inside `leadscorer:with-database` runs `run-migrations`, `seed-database`, `verify-persistence`, `uiop:quit 0`; fail-closed `uiop:quit 1` on error. Invocation: source `.env`, then `qlot exec sbcl --non-interactive --load scripts/db-setup.lisp`.

## 7. YAML config loading — status: NOT yet implemented

- No YAML library dependency exists: `:depends-on` is only `("fare-csv" "postmodern")`; qlfile has no yaml/cl-yaml/yason. Grep for `yaml`/`config` across `src/` and the `.asd` returned nothing.
- There is **no config loader** in the codebase. Model params and business rules are currently hardcoded as Lisp `defparameter`s in `scoring.lisp` (e.g. `*weight-economic*` 0.40 `:14`, `*weight-affinity*` 0.35 `:16`, `*weight-adherence*` 0.25 `:18`, `*weight-momentum*` 0.5 `:28`, `*composite-form*` `:geometric` `:32`, `*maturity-churn-multiple*`, `*dimension-floor*`, `*normalization*`, etc.).
- The YAML approach is only a stated intent in `docs/concepcao-inicial.md:131-132` and `:420` ("Parâmetros de modelo e regras de negócio (limites, pesos e afins) em arquivos YAML; lidos pela aplicação"). This is a design target for the web/application phase (task 8W2N), not existing code. The web layer will need to introduce the YAML dependency and loader itself.

---

### Quick reference — the persistence API the web layer will call
- Wrap all DB work in `(leadscorer:with-database ...)` (binds `postmodern:*database*`).
- Read data with `postmodern:query`/`postmodern:execute` using `$N` params (no S-SQL, no prepared statements, no DAO structs exist yet).
- Bootstrap/refresh schema+data: `leadscorer:run-migrations`, `leadscorer:seed-database`, `leadscorer:verify-persistence`.
- Login hierarchy tables for selection screen: `regional_offices(id,name)` → `sales_managers(id,name,username,regional_office_id)` → `sales_agents(id,name,username,sales_manager_id)`. No `sales_teams` table exists.
- Credentials come exclusively from env vars `PGDATABASE/PGUSER/PGPASSWORD/PGHOST/PGPORT`; nothing hardcoded.

## 3. Session + login

### Middleware wrapping (Lack builder)

Wrap each Ningle app with the `lack` builder DSL:
```
(lack:builder
  (:static :path "/assets/" :root <static-root>)
  :session                      ; memory store + cookie by default
  app)                          ; the ningle:app
```
- `:session` with no args uses the in-memory store and a cookie-backed state — correct for a single-image MVP. If an explicit store is wanted: `(:session :store (lack.session.store.memory:make-memory-store))`. FLAG: confirm the exact keyword and store constructor symbol under the pinned Lack; the memory store is the default so the bare `:session` form is the safe minimal choice.
- Static must be registered BEFORE session in the builder so asset requests skip session bookkeeping (minor) and so `/assets/*` short-circuits before routing. Order: static, then session, then app.

### Reading/writing the session inside a handler

The session is a hash-table placed by the middleware into the Lack env under `:lack.session`. Reach it from Ningle via the current request/context. FLAG (API uncertainty to confirm): the two candidate access paths are
- `(gethash :lack.session (lack.request:request-env ningle:*request*))`, or
- a Ningle convenience — `(ningle:context :session)` populates from that env key in recent Ningle.

Write a thin `session-table ()` accessor in `session.lisp` that returns this hash-table, isolating the uncertainty to one function. Then pure helpers on top:
- `session-put (table user-id role username)` → sets `:user-id`, `:role`, `:username` keys.
- `session-user (table)` → returns the three values or `nil`.
- `session-clear (table)` → `clrhash` (logout).
- `authenticated-p (table)` and `session-role (table)`.

Session identity/regeneration on login: if the pinned Lack exposes session-id rotation, rotate on successful login to avoid fixation; otherwise note as acceptable for MVP (FLAG).

### GET /login

Handler (per app, role captured in closure):
1. Query the seeded users for this role (see `queries.lisp`): `list-usernames :agent` → `SELECT username, name FROM sales_agents ORDER BY username`; `:manager` → same on `sales_managers`. Wrap in `ls:with-database`.
2. Render the login page via `render-login` (point 4) passing role + the username list.
3. Return the HTML string (Ningle → 200 text/html). Set `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` explicitly and attach the CSP header (point 5).

### POST /login

1. Read chosen `user` param. Ningle exposes params via the handler's `params` arg / `(ningle:context :params)` — FLAG exact accessor; the handler lambda receives a params alist in Ningle, keyed by string `"user"`.
2. Validate against the DB for THIS role only: `lookup-user :agent username` → `SELECT id FROM sales_agents WHERE username = $1` (parameterized — no interpolation). Manager app queries `sales_managers`. This is the role-segregation enforcement: an agent username submitted to the manager app returns no row and is rejected, and vice-versa.
3. On hit: `session-put` {id, role, username}; redirect 303/302 to `/` (the app home).
4. On miss (unknown or wrong-role username, or blank): re-render `/login` with an error hint (still 200, or 422). Keep it server-rendered; no JS.

### Redirect + status in Ningle — FLAG (API uncertainty)

Ningle handlers may return either a body string OR a raw Clack response list `(status headers body)`. For redirects the robust, well-documented shape is to return the Clack list directly:
```
(list 302 (list :location "/" :content-type "text/plain") (list ""))
```
Alternatively mutate `ningle:*response*` (a `lack.response` object): `(setf (lack.response:response-status ningle:*response*) 302)` and push `:location`. Recommendation: return the explicit Clack list for redirects (least API surface to get wrong); use it uniformly for setting the CSP header on HTML responses too (return `(list 200 (list* :content-type "text/html; charset=utf-8" <csp-header-plist>) (list html-string))`). Confirm the `lack.response` accessor names only if the mutate-style is chosen.

### /logout

`session-clear`, redirect to `/login`. Accept POST (a form button "Sair"); a GET logout is acceptable for MVP but POST is cleaner given `form-action 'self'` CSP.

### Auth gate

A small higher-order wrapper `require-auth (role handler)` that, before invoking `handler`, checks `authenticated-p` AND `session-role = role`; if not, returns a redirect to `/login`. Apply it to the home route (and any future protected route). Because each app only ever writes its own role into the session and only reads from its own cookie/origin (separate ports = separate cookie scope), cross-app session bleed is structurally prevented; the role check is defense-in-depth.

## 5. Static assets + CSP

### Serving statics

Use Lack's static middleware in the builder (point 3): `(:static :path "/assets/" :root <static-root>)`. Layout under `src/web/static/`:
```
static/app.css
static/htmx.min.js            (vendored htmx 2.0.x, downloaded once, checked in)
static/fonts/IBMPlexSans-Regular.woff2   ... (the six woff2, copied from .claude/assets/fonts/)
```
The six fonts must be COPIED into the served static root (the `.claude/assets/fonts` dir is design material, not a served path). Reference them from `app.css` as `/assets/fonts/...`.

MIME types: Lack's static middleware derives Content-Type from extension. Confirm `.woff2` → `font/woff2` and `.css` → `text/css` are in its type table (FLAG: older mime tables mislabel woff2; if so, either serve fonts via a tiny explicit handler that sets `font/woff2`, or configure the middleware's type map). Wrong font MIME still loads in most browsers but is worth verifying with `curl -I`.

### CSP header (emit on every HTML response; static middleware responses need it too, ideally)

Attach via a middleware or by including it in the header plist of each handler's returned Clack response. Cleanest: a tiny custom middleware wrapping the app that adds these response headers to all responses:
```
Content-Security-Policy:
  default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; font-src 'self';
  img-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'
```
Also add `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` (cheap hardening; complements the woff2 MIME concern). Put this CSP middleware OUTSIDE session/static in the builder so it covers asset responses and error responses alike.

### htmx.config.allowEval = false without inline script

htmx 2.x reads configuration from `<meta name="htmx-config" content='{...}'>` — this is static markup, not inline script, so it is CSP-clean under `script-src 'self'`. Set:
```
<meta name="htmx-config" content='{"allowEval":false,"includeIndicatorStyles":false}'>
```
- `allowEval:false` disables htmx's use of `eval`/`Function` (event filters, `hx-on` dynamic expressions), so `script-src` needs NO `'unsafe-eval'`.
- CONFIRM/PITFALL: htmx by default INJECTS an inline `<style>` for its indicator (`includeIndicatorStyles` default true). Under `style-src 'self'` (no `'unsafe-inline'`) that injection would be blocked and log a CSP violation. Setting `includeIndicatorStyles:false` prevents the injection; the indicator CSS is instead shipped in `app.css` (point 4). This is the key subtlety that makes strict `style-src 'self'` compatible with htmx.
- With `allowEval:false` + `includeIndicatorStyles:false` and htmx loaded as an external `/assets/htmx.min.js`, htmx needs neither `'unsafe-eval'` nor `'unsafe-inline'`. Confirmed by design; verify at runtime via the browser console (zero CSP violations) during vnu/manual check.

For this foundation phase htmx is merely present/loaded (no hx-* interactions yet); the requirement is that it loads under strict CSP.

## Risks & pitfalls

- **immutable-uiop no-warnings regression (highest risk).** Clack/Hunchentoot/Ningle/Lack/Spinneret each transitively depend on UIOP, Bordeaux-Threads, Alexandria, etc. The `register-immutable-system "uiop"` form MUST remain the first evaluated form in `leadscorer.asd`, before the new `defsystem`. Do the load-warnings check (step 1) in a FRESH image (`qlot exec sbcl` clean load), not an incremental one, since redefinition warnings only surface on first load. If warnings reappear, some transitive dep is reloading UIOP — the fix is the existing immutable registration, not new pins.
- **Lack session API specifics (uncertain).** Exact env key (`:lack.session`), whether to use `ningle:context :session`, and session-store constructor symbols vary across Lack versions. Isolated to one `session-table` accessor + the bare `:session` builder keyword; confirm against the pinned Lack source before wiring handlers.
- **Ningle response/redirect + params (uncertain).** Returning a raw Clack list `(status headers body)` is the most version-stable way to set 302/Location and the CSP/Content-Type headers; the mutate-`*response*` accessors (`lack.response:response-status`, `response-headers`) are the alternative. Param access is via the handler's params alist / `ningle:context`. Confirm the exact symbols; do not invent them.
- **CSP breaking htmx.** The non-obvious trap is htmx's default inline indicator `<style>` injection, blocked by `style-src 'self'`. Must set `includeIndicatorStyles:false` in the htmx-config meta and ship the indicator CSS in `app.css`. With `allowEval:false` no `'unsafe-eval'` is needed. Verify zero console CSP violations at runtime — the definitive test.
- **woff2 MIME.** Lack static middleware's type table may not map `.woff2` → `font/woff2`. Verify with `curl -I`; if wrong, serve fonts through an explicit handler that sets the type, or extend the middleware's mime map. Add `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

### Config (`config.lisp`)

Pure env readers with dev defaults:
- `agent-port` ← `LEADSCORER_AGENT_PORT`, default `8081`
- `manager-port` ← `LEADSCORER_MANAGER_PORT`, default `8082`

Use `uiop:getenv` + `parse-integer` with a defaulting helper, exactly like `database-connection-spec` does. Document each in a docstring stating the env var and default.

### App singletons + running handlers

Special vars (the "necessary singletons"):
- `*agent-app*`, `*manager-app*` — the built Ningle app objects (created lazily by `make-*-app` or at load; prefer construction in `start` to keep load side-effect-free).
- `*agent-handler*`, `*manager-handler*` — the Clack handler objects returned by `clackup`, initially `nil`.

`make-agent-app` / `make-manager-app`: construct `(make-instance 'ningle:app)` (using the library's class is allowed — the house rule bans US defining CLOS for OUR data model, not using library objects), register routes for that role, wrap with middleware, return the wrapped Clack app (a funcallable). Pass the role (`:agent` / `:manager`) as a closed-over value so the same handler code serves both apps with role-specific gating and chrome.

`start (&key agent-port manager-port)`:
- Guard against double-start (if handlers non-nil, `stop` first or error).
- `(setf *agent-handler* (clack:clackup (make-agent-app) :server :hunchentoot :port (or agent-port (agent-port)) :use-thread t :address "127.0.0.1"))` and likewise for manager. `:address "127.0.0.1"` for a dev/MVP local binding; make it configurable if needed.
- Return both ports for the caller/log.

`stop ()`:
- `(when *agent-handler* (clack:stop *agent-handler*))` then `(setf *agent-handler* nil)`, same for manager. Idempotent.

Functional style: handlers are plain functions/closures; the only mutable state is the four special vars, which are the genuine singletons (the running servers). No other globals.

## 3. Session + login

### Middleware wrapping (Lack builder)

Wrap each Ningle app with the `lack` builder DSL:
```
(lack:builder
  (:static :path "/assets/" :root <static-root>)
  :session                      ; memory store + cookie by default
  app)                          ; the ningle:app
```
- `:session` with no args uses the in-memory store and a cookie-backed state — correct for a single-image MVP. If an explicit store is wanted: `(:session :store (lack.session.store.memory:make-memory-store))`. FLAG: confirm the exact keyword and store constructor symbol under the pinned Lack; the memory store is the default so the bare `:session` form is the safe minimal choice.
- Static must be registered BEFORE session in the builder so asset requests skip session bookkeeping (minor) and so `/assets/*` short-circuits before routing. Order: static, then session, then app.

### Reading/writing the session inside a handler

The session is a hash-table placed by the middleware into the Lack env under `:lack.session`. Reach it from Ningle via the current request/context. FLAG (API uncertainty to confirm): the two candidate access paths are
- `(gethash :lack.session (lack.request:request-env ningle:*request*))`, or
- a Ningle convenience — `(ningle:context :session)` populates from that env key in recent Ningle.

Write a thin `session-table ()` accessor in `session.lisp` that returns this hash-table, isolating the uncertainty to one function. Then pure helpers on top:
- `session-put (table user-id role username)` → sets `:user-id`, `:role`, `:username` keys.
- `session-user (table)` → returns the three values or `nil`.
- `session-clear (table)` → `clrhash` (logout).
- `authenticated-p (table)` and `session-role (table)`.

Session identity/regeneration on login: if the pinned Lack exposes session-id rotation, rotate on successful login to avoid fixation; otherwise note as acceptable for MVP (FLAG).

### GET /login

Handler (per app, role captured in closure):
1. Query the seeded users for this role (see `queries.lisp`): `list-usernames :agent` → `SELECT username, name FROM sales_agents ORDER BY username`; `:manager` → same on `sales_managers`. Wrap in `ls:with-database`.
2. Render the login page via `render-login` (point 4) passing role + the username list.
3. Return the HTML string (Ningle → 200 text/html). Set `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` explicitly and attach the CSP header (point 5).

### POST /login

1. Read chosen `user` param. Ningle exposes params via the handler's `params` arg / `(ningle:context :params)` — FLAG exact accessor; the handler lambda receives a params alist in Ningle, keyed by string `"user"`.
2. Validate against the DB for THIS role only: `lookup-user :agent username` → `SELECT id FROM sales_agents WHERE username = $1` (parameterized — no interpolation). Manager app queries `sales_managers`. This is the role-segregation enforcement: an agent username submitted to the manager app returns no row and is rejected, and vice-versa.
3. On hit: `session-put` {id, role, username}; redirect 303/302 to `/` (the app home).
4. On miss (unknown or wrong-role username, or blank): re-render `/login` with an error hint (still 200, or 422). Keep it server-rendered; no JS.

### Redirect + status in Ningle — FLAG (API uncertainty)

Ningle handlers may return either a body string OR a raw Clack response list `(status headers body)`. For redirects the robust, well-documented shape is to return the Clack list directly:
```
(list 302 (list :location "/" :content-type "text/plain") (list ""))
```
Alternatively mutate `ningle:*response*` (a `lack.response` object): `(setf (lack.response:response-status ningle:*response*) 302)` and push `:location`. Recommendation: return the explicit Clack list for redirects (least API surface to get wrong); use it uniformly for setting the CSP header on HTML responses too (return `(list 200 (list* :content-type "text/html; charset=utf-8" <csp-header-plist>) (list html-string))`). Confirm the `lack.response` accessor names only if the mutate-style is chosen.

### /logout

`session-clear`, redirect to `/login`. Accept POST (a form button "Sair"); a GET logout is acceptable for MVP but POST is cleaner given `form-action 'self'` CSP.

### Auth gate

A small higher-order wrapper `require-auth (role handler)` that, before invoking `handler`, checks `authenticated-p` AND `session-role = role`; if not, returns a redirect to `/login`. Apply it to the home route (and any future protected route). Because each app only ever writes its own role into the session and only reads from its own cookie/origin (separate ports = separate cookie scope), cross-app session bleed is structurally prevented; the role check is defense-in-depth.

## 5. Static assets + CSP

### Serving statics

Use Lack's static middleware in the builder (point 3): `(:static :path "/assets/" :root <static-root>)`. Layout under `src/web/static/`:
```
static/app.css
static/htmx.min.js            (vendored htmx 2.0.x, downloaded once, checked in)
static/fonts/IBMPlexSans-Regular.woff2   ... (the six woff2, copied from .claude/assets/fonts/)
```
The six fonts must be COPIED into the served static root (the `.claude/assets/fonts` dir is design material, not a served path). Reference them from `app.css` as `/assets/fonts/...`.

MIME types: Lack's static middleware derives Content-Type from extension. Confirm `.woff2` → `font/woff2` and `.css` → `text/css` are in its type table (FLAG: older mime tables mislabel woff2; if so, either serve fonts via a tiny explicit handler that sets `font/woff2`, or configure the middleware's type map). Wrong font MIME still loads in most browsers but is worth verifying with `curl -I`.

### CSP header (emit on every HTML response; static middleware responses need it too, ideally)

Attach via a middleware or by including it in the header plist of each handler's returned Clack response. Cleanest: a tiny custom middleware wrapping the app that adds these response headers to all responses:
```
Content-Security-Policy:
  default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; font-src 'self';
  img-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'
```
Also add `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` (cheap hardening; complements the woff2 MIME concern). Put this CSP middleware OUTSIDE session/static in the builder so it covers asset responses and error responses alike.

### htmx.config.allowEval = false without inline script

htmx 2.x reads configuration from `<meta name="htmx-config" content='{...}'>` — this is static markup, not inline script, so it is CSP-clean under `script-src 'self'`. Set:
```
<meta name="htmx-config" content='{"allowEval":false,"includeIndicatorStyles":false}'>
```
- `allowEval:false` disables htmx's use of `eval`/`Function` (event filters, `hx-on` dynamic expressions), so `script-src` needs NO `'unsafe-eval'`.
- CONFIRM/PITFALL: htmx by default INJECTS an inline `<style>` for its indicator (`includeIndicatorStyles` default true). Under `style-src 'self'` (no `'unsafe-inline'`) that injection would be blocked and log a CSP violation. Setting `includeIndicatorStyles:false` prevents the injection; the indicator CSS is instead shipped in `app.css` (point 4). This is the key subtlety that makes strict `style-src 'self'` compatible with htmx.
- With `allowEval:false` + `includeIndicatorStyles:false` and htmx loaded as an external `/assets/htmx.min.js`, htmx needs neither `'unsafe-eval'` nor `'unsafe-inline'`. Confirmed by design; verify at runtime via the browser console (zero CSP violations) during vnu/manual check.

For this foundation phase htmx is merely present/loaded (no hx-* interactions yet); the requirement is that it loads under strict CSP.

O terceiro objetivo específico do LeadScorer é a interface web (tarefa-pai 8W2N). A Fase 1

precondição de todas as telas de negócio, isolada num incremento coerente e verificável. Não

  seu handler Clack/Hunchentoot em porta dedicada, no mesmo processo Lisp. Isolamento de sessão
  por origem (cookie por porta). Fiel a "cada aplicação em seu endereço" (ADR D2K9). Registro no
  worklog; não demanda novo ADR, pois é detalhe de implementação dentro de D2K9.

  vendorizado localmente** como ativo estático (sem CDN).

Entra: sistema/pacote web; dois apps Ningle em duas portas (Hunchentoot via Clack); layout base
Spinneret reproduzindo o chrome dos protótipos (appbar de login e navbar com hambúrguer CSS);
CSS estático consolidado + fontes + htmx servidos sob CSP estrita; login por seleção do usuário
semeado (GET/POST /login), sessão de servidor (Lack), logout e portão de autenticação por papel.

  biblioteca, `ningle:app`, é permitido).
- Credenciais só por variáveis de ambiente (`PG*`), como já faz `src/db.lisp`. Portas por
  ambiente com defaults de desenvolvimento.
- Toda leitura de dados dentro de `leadscorer:with-database`. Login consulta `sales_agents` /
  `sales_managers` (coluna `username`, dot-slug tipo `anna.snelling` — a fonte é o banco, não os
  hifens dos protótipos).

topo, que garante carga sem avisos) os sistemas:

  "ningle" "spinneret")`, `:serial t`, módulo `src/web/`.

1. `package.lisp` — pacote `#:leadscorer.web`, `(:use #:cl)`, `(:local-nicknames (#:ls
   #:leadscorer))`; exporta `start`, `stop`, `*agent-app*`, `*manager-app*`, `make-agent-app`,
   `make-manager-app`.
2. `config.lisp` — leitores de ambiente: `agent-port` (`LEADSCORER_AGENT_PORT`, default 8081),
   `manager-port` (default 8082), `static-root` (`asdf:system-relative-pathname`).
3. `render.lisp` — layout base Spinneret (função/macro com corpo, não CLOS): `<head>` fixo

   `<meta name=htmx-config content='{"allowEval":false,"includeIndicatorStyles":false}'>`,
   `<script src=/assets/htmx.min.js defer>`); `render-appbar`, `render-navbar` (hambúrguer CSS,
   `.role` só no gerente, aba "Início" ativa — sem links mortos a telas ainda não construídas),

6. `handlers.lisp` — GET/POST `/login`, POST `/logout`, home, e `require-auth` (portão que exige

   `*agent-handler*`/`*manager-handler*` dos handlers Clack em execução.

Ativos estáticos em `src/web/static/`: `app.css` (consolidado dos protótipos: `:root` de tokens
Gray 100, `@font-face` reescritos para `/assets/fonts/...`, appbar, navbar+hambúrguer+`@media
max-width:820px`, card, select, btn, hint, footer, padding centrado do navbar, e uma regra

resposta. CSP: `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; font-src 'self';
img-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`.

Dependências: acrescentar ao `qlfile` as linhas `ql clack`, `ql clack-handler-hunchentoot`,
`ql lack`, `ql ningle`, `ql spinneret`; regenerar `qlfile.lock` com `qlot install` sob a dist

4. **Sessão (red→green).** Testes puros dos helpers e do portão por papel; implementar
   `session.lisp`. Commit.
5. **Queries (gated por PG).** `queries.lisp`; testes com contagens canônicas (35 agentes, 6

6. **Handlers e server (red→green).** `handlers.lisp` e `server.lisp`; testes de requisição via
   `clack.test`/`lack/test` (GET /login 200 sem PG pela indireção `*list-usernames-fn*`,

   conferir MIME das woff2 (`curl -I`). Commit.

- **Regressão de avisos (uiop imutável) — risco maior.** Clack/Hunchentoot/Ningle/Lack/Spinneret

- **Discrepância protótipo x banco**: renderizar dot-slugs do banco, não os hifens dos

;;;; config.lisp --- Configuração de ambiente da camada web do LeadScorer.

(in-package #:leadscorer/web)

;;; A configuração operacional (portas de escuta, endereço de vínculo e raiz
;;; dos ativos estáticos) é lida de variáveis de ambiente, com valores padrão
;;; de desenvolvimento. Nenhum segredo é lido aqui; as credenciais do banco
;;; permanecem confinadas a 'src/db.lisp' e às variáveis PG*.

(defun env-integer (name default)
  "Retorna o inteiro da variável de ambiente NAME ou DEFAULT quando ausente ou
vazia. Sinaliza um erro quando o valor presente não é um inteiro, de modo que
uma configuração inválida falhe de imediato em vez de silenciosamente."
  (let ((value (uiop:getenv name)))
    (if (or (null value) (string= value ""))
        default
        (handler-case (parse-integer value)
          (error ()
            (error "A variável de ambiente ~A não é um inteiro válido: ~S."
                   name value))))))

(defun env-string (name default)
  "Retorna o valor da variável de ambiente NAME ou DEFAULT quando ausente ou
vazia."
  (let ((value (uiop:getenv name)))
    (if (or (null value) (string= value ""))
        default
        value)))

(defun agent-port ()
  "Porta de escuta da aplicação do agente (LEADSCORER_AGENT_PORT, padrão 8081)."
  (env-integer "LEADSCORER_AGENT_PORT" 8081))

(defun manager-port ()
  "Porta de escuta da aplicação do gerente (LEADSCORER_MANAGER_PORT, padrão
8082)."
  (env-integer "LEADSCORER_MANAGER_PORT" 8082))

(defun bind-address ()
  "Endereço de vínculo dos servidores (LEADSCORER_BIND_ADDRESS, padrão
127.0.0.1, restrito ao laço local no desenvolvimento)."
  (env-string "LEADSCORER_BIND_ADDRESS" "127.0.0.1"))

(defun static-root ()
  "Diretório físico dos ativos estáticos servidos sob '/assets/', a saber,
'src/web/static/' relativo à raiz do sistema."
  (asdf:system-relative-pathname :leadscorer/web "src/web/static/"))

;;;; render.lisp --- Layout base e páginas em Spinneret da camada web.

(in-package #:leadscorer/web)

;;; O layout base reproduz o chrome dos protótipos autônomos de
;;; '.claude/assets/examples/' (tema escuro Gray 100), servindo o CSS e o HTMX
;;; como ativos estáticos sob CSP estrita. Spinneret escapa o texto por padrão,
;;; de modo que os nomes de usuário vindos do banco são escapados sem ação
;;; adicional. As funções auxiliares emitem no fluxo Spinneret corrente
;;; ('spinneret:with-html'); as funções de página retornam a string completa
;;; ('spinneret:with-html-string').

(defparameter +htmx-config+
  "{\"allowEval\":false,\"includeIndicatorStyles\":false}"
  "Configuração do HTMX embutida como meta estática, não como script inline, de
modo a permanecer compatível com a CSP 'script-src 'self''. Desliga 'eval'
(dispensa 'unsafe-eval') e a injeção do estilo de indicador (que o
'style-src 'self'' bloquearia; o estilo reside em 'app.css').")

(defun role-scope (role)
  "Texto do escopo de aplicação exibido no chrome, por papel."
  (ecase role
    (:agent "Aplicação do agente")
    (:manager "Aplicação do gerente")))

(defun role-field-label (role)
  "Rótulo do campo de seleção de usuário, por papel."
  (ecase role
    (:agent "Agente de vendas")
    (:manager "Gerente de vendas")))

(defun role-placeholder (role)
  "Texto da opção inicial desabilitada do seletor, por papel."
  (ecase role
    (:agent "Escolha um agente")
    (:manager "Escolha um gerente")))

(defun role-context (role)
  "Substantivo do papel para títulos e sub-rótulos."
  (ecase role
    (:agent "agente")
    (:manager "gerente")))

(defun role-hint (role)
  "Nota recíproca informando que a outra aplicação é servida em endereço
próprio, com a mesma identificação, sem gestão de papéis."
  (ecase role
    (:agent
     "A aplicação do gerente é servida em endereço próprio, com a mesma forma
de identificação. As duas aplicações são segregadas, sem gestão de papéis.")
    (:manager
     "A aplicação do agente é servida em endereço próprio, com a mesma forma
de identificação. As duas aplicações são segregadas, sem gestão de papéis.")))

(defun render-head (title)
  "Emite o <head> comum: metadados, título, folha de estilo estática e a
configuração e o carregamento do HTMX como ativo estático."
  (spinneret:with-html
    (:head
     (:meta :charset "utf-8")
     (:meta :name "viewport" :content "width=device-width, initial-scale=1")
     (:title title)
     (:link :rel "stylesheet" :href "/assets/app.css")
     (:meta :name "htmx-config" :content +htmx-config+)
     (:script :src "/assets/htmx.min.js" :defer t))))

(defun render-footer ()
  "Emite o rodapé comum das páginas."
  (spinneret:with-html
    (:footer "LeadScorer --- MVP de classificação e priorização de leads")))

(defun render-appbar (role)
  "Emite a faixa superior mínima das telas de login, com o wordmark e o escopo
da aplicação."
  (spinneret:with-html
    (:header :class "appbar"
             (:span :class "wordmark" "LeadScorer")
             (:span :class "scope" (role-scope role)))))

(defun render-navbar (role username)
  "Emite a barra de navegação autenticada, com o menu responsivo por alternância
CSS pura, o wordmark (com a tag de papel no gerente), a aba inicial, o nome de
usuário da sessão e o botão de saída como formulário POST."
  (spinneret:with-html
    (:nav :class "navbar"
          (:input :type "checkbox" :id "nav" :class "nav-cb"
                  :aria-label "Abrir menu")
          (:label :class "nav-toggle" :for "nav"
                  (:span) (:span) (:span))
          (:span :class "brand" "LeadScorer"
                 (when (eq role :manager)
                   (spinneret:with-html (:span :class "role" "gerente"))))
          (:div :class "nav-tabs"
                (:a :href "/" :class "active" "Início"))
          (:div :class "nav-right"
                (:span :class "user-pill" username)
                (:span :class "pill" (:span :class "dot") "Sessão ativa")
                (:form :class "logout-form" :method "post" :action "/logout"
                       (:button :class "btn btn-sm" :type "submit" "Sair"))))))

(defun render-login-page (role usernames &optional error-message)
  "Retorna a string HTML da tela de identificação por seleção, por papel.
USERNAMES é a lista de nomes de usuário semeados a oferecer; ERROR-MESSAGE,
quando fornecida, é exibida acima do formulário. O formulário submete por POST
a '/login'."
  (spinneret:with-html-string
    (:doctype)
    (:html :lang "pt-BR"
           (render-head (format nil "LeadScorer --- Identificação (~A)"
                                (role-context role)))
           (:body
            (render-appbar role)
            (:main :class "login-main"
                   (:div :class "card"
                         (:h1 "Identificação")
                         (:p :class "lead"
                             "Selecione o seu nome de usuário para iniciar a "
                             "sessão. O acesso é por seleção, sem senha, "
                             "restrito aos usuários semeados.")
                         (when error-message
                           (spinneret:with-html
                             (:p :class "error" error-message)))
                         (:form :method "post" :action "/login"
                                (:div :class "field"
                                      (:label :for "user" (role-field-label role))
                                      (:span :class "select"
                                             (:select :id "user" :name "user"
                                                      (:option :value "" :disabled t
                                                               :selected t
                                                               (role-placeholder role))
                                                      (dolist (u usernames)
                                                        (spinneret:with-html
                                                          (:option :value u u))))))
                                (:button :class "btn btn-primary btn-block"
                                         :type "submit" "Entrar"))
                         (:p :class "hint" (role-hint role))))
            (render-footer)))))

(defun render-home-page (role username)
  "Retorna a string HTML da tela inicial autenticada de cada aplicação. Nesta
fase, a tela apresenta o chrome autenticado e um conteúdo de reserva; o painel
de indicadores e as listas são objeto das entregas seguintes."
  (spinneret:with-html-string
    (:doctype)
    (:html :lang "pt-BR"
           (render-head (format nil "LeadScorer --- Início (~A)"
                                (role-context role)))
           (:body
            (render-navbar role username)
            (:main :class "page"
                   (:div :class "page-head"
                         (:h1 "Início")
                         (:span :class "sub"
                                (format nil "~A ~A" (role-context role) username)))
                   (:p :class "placeholder"
                       "A sua sessão está ativa. O painel de indicadores e as "
                       "listas de oportunidades serão apresentados nas entregas "
                       "seguintes desta aplicação."))
            (render-footer)))))

;;;; session.lisp --- Sessão de servidor e portão de autorização por papel.

(in-package #:leadscorer/web)

;;; O middleware de sessão do Lack coloca a tabela de sessão no ambiente da
;;; requisição sob a chave :LACK.SESSION. O acessor 'session-table' isola essa
;;; dependência de API num único ponto; os demais auxiliares operam sobre a
;;; tabela e são puros, testáveis sem servidor nem banco. As chaves da sessão
;;; são palavras-chave.

(defun session-table ()
  "Retorna a tabela de sessão da requisição Ningle corrente, colocada pelo
middleware de sessão do Lack sob :LACK.SESSION no ambiente da requisição."
  (getf (lack/request:request-env ningle:*request*) :lack.session))

(defun session-put (table user-id role username)
  "Grava a identidade autenticada na sessão TABLE: identificador USER-ID, papel
ROLE (:agent ou :manager) e nome de usuário USERNAME. Retorna TABLE."
  (setf (gethash :user-id table) user-id
        (gethash :role table) role
        (gethash :username table) username)
  table)

(defun session-user (table)
  "Retorna, como valores múltiplos, o identificador, o papel e o nome de usuário
gravados na sessão TABLE, ou NIL quando a sessão não está autenticada."
  (let ((id (gethash :user-id table)))
    (when id
      (values id (gethash :role table) (gethash :username table)))))

(defun authenticated-p (table)
  "Retorna T quando a sessão TABLE contém uma identidade autenticada."
  (and (gethash :user-id table) t))

(defun session-role (table)
  "Retorna o papel gravado na sessão TABLE (:agent, :manager) ou NIL."
  (gethash :role table))

(defun session-clear (table)
  "Remove toda a identidade da sessão TABLE (logout). Retorna TABLE."
  (clrhash table)
  table)

(defun role-authorized-p (table role)
  "Retorna T quando a sessão TABLE está autenticada e o seu papel é ROLE. É o
portão de autorização por papel de cada aplicação."
  (and (authenticated-p table)
       (eq (session-role table) role)))

;;;; queries.lisp --- Consultas de identificação por seleção.

(in-package #:leadscorer/web)

;;; As consultas de login leem os usuários semeados e validam a seleção contra
;;; o banco, sempre restritas ao papel da aplicação corrente, o que reforça a
;;; segregação: um nome de usuário do papel oposto não encontra linha e é
;;; recusado. O nome de usuário é entrada externa e trafega como parâmetro
;;; vinculado ($1); a tabela é escolhida por ECASE sobre o papel interno, nunca
;;; interpolada. As indireções '*list-usernames-fn*' e '*lookup-user-fn*'
;;; permitem exercitar as rotas sem um banco vivo nos testes.

(defun db-list-usernames (role)
  "Retorna a lista dos nomes de usuário semeados do papel ROLE (:agent ou
:manager), em ordem alfabética, lida do banco."
  (ls:with-database
    (ecase role
      (:agent
       (postmodern:query
        "SELECT username FROM sales_agents ORDER BY username" :column))
      (:manager
       (postmodern:query
        "SELECT username FROM sales_managers ORDER BY username" :column)))))

(defvar *list-usernames-fn* 'db-list-usernames
  "Função que lista os nomes de usuário de um papel. Vinculável nos testes para
dispensar um banco vivo.")

(defun list-usernames (role)
  "Retorna a lista dos nomes de usuário oferecidos no login do papel ROLE."
  (funcall *list-usernames-fn* role))

(defun db-lookup-user (role username)
  "Retorna o identificador do usuário do papel ROLE cujo nome de usuário é
USERNAME, ou NIL quando não existe tal usuário nesse papel."
  (ls:with-database
    (ecase role
      (:agent
       (postmodern:query
        "SELECT id FROM sales_agents WHERE username = $1" username :single))
      (:manager
       (postmodern:query
        "SELECT id FROM sales_managers WHERE username = $1" username :single)))))

(defvar *lookup-user-fn* 'db-lookup-user
  "Função que valida um nome de usuário de um papel. Vinculável nos testes para
dispensar um banco vivo.")

(defun lookup-user (role username)
  "Retorna o identificador do usuário do papel ROLE com nome USERNAME, ou NIL
quando a seleção é inválida ou pertence ao papel oposto."
  (funcall *lookup-user-fn* role username))

;;;; queries.lisp --- Testes das consultas de login (integração com PostgreSQL).

(in-package #:leadscorer/web/tests)

;;; Estes testes exigem um PostgreSQL alcançável e semeado. Seguem a convenção
;;; da suíte de persistência: quando o banco não está disponível, o teste é
;;; ignorado ('skip') de modo que a suíte permaneça verde sem banco. As
;;; contagens canônicas (35 agentes, 6 gerentes) residem em 'src/verify.lisp'.

(define-test list-usernames-and-lookup-live
  "Lista os usuários semeados por papel e valida a segregação na busca."
  (if (ls::database-reachable-p)
      (progn
        (ls:with-database
          (ls:run-migrations)
          (ls:seed-database))
        (let ((agents (web::list-usernames :agent))
              (managers (web::list-usernames :manager)))
          (is = 35 (length agents))
          (is = 6 (length managers))
          ;; Um nome de agente é validado no papel de agente e recusado no de
          ;; gerente, e vice-versa: a segregação por papel na própria consulta.
          (let ((agent-name (first agents))
                (manager-name (first managers)))
            (true (integerp (web::lookup-user :agent agent-name)))
            (is eql nil (web::lookup-user :manager agent-name))
            (true (integerp (web::lookup-user :manager manager-name)))
            (is eql nil (web::lookup-user :agent manager-name)))
          ;; Uma seleção inexistente é recusada.
          (is eql nil (web::lookup-user :agent "inexistente.ninguem"))))
      (skip "PostgreSQL indisponível; teste de integração de login ignorado.")))

;;;; handlers.lisp --- Respostas e lógica de rota das aplicações web.

(in-package #:leadscorer/web)

;;; A lógica de cada rota reside em funções núcleo com sufixo '-for', que
;;; recebem a tabela de sessão explicitamente e, portanto, são testáveis sem
;;; servidor nem banco (vinculando '*list-usernames-fn*' e '*lookup-user-fn*').
;;; Os finos invólucros de rota Ningle, em 'server.lisp', apenas fornecem a
;;; tabela de sessão corrente via 'session-table'.

(defun html-response (html &optional (status 200))
  "Constrói uma resposta Clack de HTML a partir da string HTML, com o corpo
codificado em UTF-8 (octetos), de modo que os acentos do português sejam
transmitidos sem ambiguidade de codificação."
  (list status
        (list :content-type "text/html; charset=utf-8")
        (sb-ext:string-to-octets html :external-format :utf-8)))

(defun redirect (location &optional (status 302))
  "Constrói uma resposta Clack de redirecionamento para LOCATION."
  (list status (list :location location) (list "")))

(defun login-page-response (role &optional error-message)
  "Resposta da tela de login do papel ROLE, com os usuários semeados e, quando
fornecida, uma ERROR-MESSAGE."
  (html-response (render-login-page role (list-usernames role) error-message)))

(defun login-submit-for (role table params)
  "Processa a submissão do login do papel ROLE com os parâmetros PARAMS,
gravando a identidade na sessão TABLE e redirecionando à home quando a seleção
é válida para o papel, ou re-renderizando o login com erro caso contrário. A
validação é restrita ao papel, o que recusa um nome de usuário do papel oposto."
  (let* ((username (cdr (assoc "user" params :test #'string=)))
         (id (and username (plusp (length username)) (lookup-user role username))))
    (if id
        (progn
          (session-put table id role username)
          (redirect "/"))
        (login-page-response
         role "Seleção inválida. Escolha um usuário da lista."))))

(defun logout-response-for (table)
  "Encerra a sessão TABLE e redireciona ao login."
  (when table (session-clear table))
  (redirect "/login"))

(defun home-response-for (role table)
  "Resposta da tela inicial do papel ROLE quando a sessão TABLE está autorizada
para esse papel; caso contrário, redireciona ao login (portão de autenticação)."
  (if (and table (role-authorized-p table role))
      (multiple-value-bind (id session-role username) (session-user table)
        (declare (ignore id session-role))

;;;; server.lisp --- Construção e ciclo de vida das duas aplicações web.

(in-package #:leadscorer/web)

;;; As duas aplicações, do agente e do gerente, são apps Ningle distintos,
;;; servidos por handlers Clack/Hunchentoot em portas próprias, no mesmo
;;; processo. A segregação é por origem: cada porta tem o seu próprio cookie de
;;; sessão. Cada app é envolvido pela mesma pilha de middleware: o cabeçalho de
;;; segurança (CSP estrita e nosniff) no topo, cobrindo inclusive os ativos e as
;;; respostas de erro; a seguir os ativos estáticos sob '/assets/'; e a sessão.

(defparameter +content-security-policy+
  (concatenate 'string
               "default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; "
               "font-src 'self'; img-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; "
               "form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'")
  "Política de segurança de conteúdo estrita. Autoriza apenas ativos de mesma
origem; dispensa 'unsafe-inline' e 'unsafe-eval' porque o CSS e o HTMX são
servidos como ativos estáticos e o HTMX opera com 'allowEval' em falso.")

(defun add-security-headers (response)
  "Acrescenta a CSP estrita e 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' aos cabeçalhos
de RESPONSE, uma resposta Clack (status cabeçalhos corpo)."
  (destructuring-bind (status headers body) response
    (list status
          (append headers
                  (list :content-security-policy +content-security-policy+
                        :x-content-type-options "nosniff"))
          body)))

(defun security-headers-middleware (app)
  "Middleware Lack que aplica os cabeçalhos de segurança a toda resposta de
APP."
  (lambda (env)
    (add-security-headers (funcall app env))))

(defun make-app (role)
  "Constrói a aplicação web do papel ROLE (:agent ou :manager): um app Ningle
com as rotas de login, logout e home, envolvido pela pilha de middleware de
segurança, ativos estáticos e sessão. Retorna o app Clack funcallable."
  (let ((app (make-instance 'ningle:app)))
    (setf (ningle:route app "/login" :method :get)
          (lambda (params)
            (declare (ignore params))
            (login-page-response role)))
    (setf (ningle:route app "/login" :method :post)
          (lambda (params)
            (login-submit-for role (session-table) params)))
    (setf (ningle:route app "/logout" :method :post)
          (lambda (params)
            (declare (ignore params))
            (logout-response-for (session-table))))
    (setf (ningle:route app "/" :method :get)
          (lambda (params)
            (declare (ignore params))
            (home-response-for role (session-table))))
    (lack:builder
     #'security-headers-middleware
     (:static :path "/assets/" :root (static-root))
     :session
     app)))

(defun make-agent-app ()
  "Constrói a aplicação do agente."
  (make-app :agent))

(defun make-manager-app ()
  "Constrói a aplicação do gerente."
  (make-app :manager))

(defvar *agent-app* nil
  "A aplicação Clack do agente em execução, ou NIL quando parada.")

(defvar *manager-app* nil
  "A aplicação Clack do gerente em execução, ou NIL quando parada.")

(defvar *agent-handler* nil
  "O handler Clack do servidor do agente, ou NIL quando parado.")

(defvar *manager-handler* nil
  "O handler Clack do servidor do gerente, ou NIL quando parado.")

(defun start (&key (agent-port (agent-port)) (manager-port (manager-port))
                   (address (bind-address)))
  "Inicia os dois servidores, do agente e do gerente, em portas distintas,
vinculados a ADDRESS. Sinaliza um erro se já estiverem em execução. Retorna,
como valores, as duas portas."
  (when (or *agent-handler* *manager-handler*)
    (error "Os servidores já estão em execução; chame STOP antes de reiniciar."))
  (setf *agent-app* (make-agent-app)
        *manager-app* (make-manager-app))
  (setf *agent-handler*
        (clack:clackup *agent-app* :server :hunchentoot
                                   :port agent-port :address address
                                   :use-thread t))
  (setf *manager-handler*
        (clack:clackup *manager-app* :server :hunchentoot
                                     :port manager-port :address address
                                     :use-thread t))
  (values agent-port manager-port))

(defun stop ()
  "Para os dois servidores, se em execução, e zera os handlers. Idempotente."
  (when *agent-handler*
    (clack:stop *agent-handler*)
    (setf *agent-handler* nil *agent-app* nil))
  (when *manager-handler*
    (clack:stop *manager-handler*)
    (setf *manager-handler* nil *manager-app* nil))
  (values))

;;;; run-web.lisp --- Sobe as duas aplicações web para verificação manual.
;;;;
;;;; Invocação (a partir da raiz do projeto, com o PostgreSQL provisionado):
;;;;   set -a; . ./.env; set +a

;;;; LEADSCORER_MANAGER_PORT (padrões 8081 e 8082). O login lê os usuários
;;;; semeados, de modo que o banco deve estar de pé e semeado. Encerre com
;;;; Ctrl-C, que para os dois servidores de forma ordenada.

(require :asdf)

(asdf:load-system :leadscorer/web)

(multiple-value-bind (agent-port manager-port) (leadscorer/web:start)

  (sb-sys:interactive-interrupt ()
    (format t "~&Encerrando os servidores...~%")
    (finish-output)
    (leadscorer/web:stop)

- 'docs/concepcao-inicial.md' (estorias de identificacao e acesso, arquitetura server-side);

Context cut observed: I read only the diff, the touched source files, the schema/migrations, and the permitted rules/spec/ADR. I did not open the worklog, plans, sessions or the task file.

## A) Per-criterion verdict

**Criterion 1 — Two apps compile clean and serve the themed base layout (Gray 100, local IBM Plex, design-system conformant): MET (with an evidence caveat).**
- `render.lisp` builds both pages; `role-scope`/`role-context` (render.lisp:35-52) differentiate agent vs manager. Dark-theme tokens are embedded in `app.css:690-703` and mirror `.claude/assets/tokens/dark-theme-tokens.css` exactly (`--bg-base:#161616` etc.). Six IBM Plex woff2 faces are vendored and `@font-face`'d locally (`app.css:663-687`), satisfying design.md's local-fonts rule. No `box-shadow`/glow; elevation is by layered bg + hairline borders, per design.md.
- Caveat: the automated suite renders strings and validates them with vnu, but the *served* layout (real Hunchentoot response, static middleware resolving `/assets/*`) is exercised only by the manual `run-web.lisp`. See Finding 1.

**Criterion 2 — HTMX 2.0.x served static under strict CSP with `allowEval:false`: MET.**
- Vendored file is htmx `version:"2.0.4"` (confirmed in `src/web/static/htmx.min.js`). Loaded as same-origin static asset `/assets/htmx.min.js` (render.lisp:65). Config is delivered as a `<meta name="htmx-config">` tag (render.lisp:64, value `+htmx-config+` render.lisp:19-20) with `allowEval:false` — not an inline script, so it survives `script-src 'self'`. CSP (`server.lisp:26-31`) carries no `unsafe-inline`/`unsafe-eval`. Consistent and correct. One latent gap for the next phase — see Finding 3.

**Criterion 3 — Passwordless selection login sets the correct server session per role; apps segregated (no role management): MET at the logic layer; end-to-end unproven.**
- Segregation is enforced twice, fail-closed: (a) the login query is role-scoped by `ecase` selecting `sales_agents` vs `sales_managers` (queries.lisp:15-23, 33-43), so an opposite-role username finds no row and is rejected; (b) the home gate `role-authorized-p` (session.lisp:39-43) requires the session role to `eq` the app's role, so an agent-role session hitting the manager app is redirected to `/login` (handlers.lisp:47-53). `username` is bound as `$1`, never interpolated. Login input is validated and empty/missing/unknown all funnel to the error page (handlers.lisp:33-38). Verified against schema: `username TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` on both tables (`db/migrations/0001_reference.sql:21,28`), so the `:single` lookup is safe.
- Two reservations: the real cookie/session round-trip and ningle POST-param shape are not covered by automated tests (Finding 1), and the two apps share a session-cookie name on a shared host (Finding 2).

**Criterion 4 — Base layout responsive on iPhone 13 (navbar collapse): MET.**
- `@media (max-width:820px)` reveals `.nav-toggle` and hides `.nav-tabs`, restored via the pure-CSS `.nav-cb:checked ~ .nav-tabs` toggle (app.css:862-873); the checkbox precedes `.nav-tabs` as a sibling in `render-navbar` (render.lisp:84-92), so the selector is valid. A second breakpoint at 560px tightens padding. The checkbox carries `aria-label`. 390px falls inside the 820px breakpoint.

**Criterion 5 — Applicable software verification passes: MET (asserted precondition, not re-run).**

## B) Findings (most severe first)

**1 — MEDIUM — automated suite verifies route logic but not the live session/POST round-trip.**
`tests/web/*` drive the `-for` cores with a hand-built `fresh-session` hash-table (session.lisp test:1126) and stub `*lookup-user-fn*`/`*list-usernames-fn*`. This proves the gate/redirect/mutation logic, but three integration points that Criterion 3 actually requires are unexercised: (a) that Lack persists the in-place-mutated session hash-table and emits `Set-Cookie` on the 302 (handlers.lisp:36-38 relies on it); (b) that ningle delivers POST body params as the string-keyed alist `login-submit-for` assumes at `(assoc "user" params :test #'string=)` (handlers.lisp:33) — if ningle's shape differs, login silently always fails to the error page; (c) that the static middleware resolves `/assets/app.css|htmx.min.js|fonts/*`. This is the classic pass-while-checking-something-narrower gap. *Remediation:* make human sign-off contingent on a `run-web.lisp` walk-through — login→home→logout on *both* apps, plus a cross-role attempt — and record the observation; optionally add one Clack integration test that issues a real request against a booted app.

**2 — MEDIUM — both apps use the same session cookie name on a shared host, so they collide on localhost.**

This phase ships no `hx-*` AJAX attributes, so Criterion 2 is fully met, but the next phase's first `hx-get` will be blocked. Latent coupling worth recording now. *Remediation:* add `connect-src 'self'` when AJAX is introduced.

**4 — LOW — partial-start leaves an inconsistent handler state.**

**5 — LOW — `role-authorized-p`/`authenticated-p` assume a non-nil session table.**
`authenticated-p` (session.lisp:26-28) calls `gethash` on `table` without a nil guard; it is safe today only because both call sites (`home-response-for` handlers.lisp:50, `logout-response-for` handlers.lisp:44) guard `table` first, and the Lack middleware always supplies one. Noted for defense-in-depth; no action required for this phase.

No high-severity findings. Secrets: none hardcoded — `config.lisp` reads only ports/bind/static-root from env with dev defaults and explicitly confines DB credentials to `src/db.lisp`/`PG*` (config.lisp:5-8), satisfying security-by-design. CLOS: only the library class `ningle:app` is instantiated (server.lisp:516); no project-owned `defclass`/`defgeneric`/`defmethod`, per CLAUDE.md. - The asserted automatic verification (compile-clean, mallet, Parachute 68+102, vnu) — taken as a satisfied precondition, not re-run.

- Visual/pixel fidelity to the `.claude/assets/examples/` prototypes (no rendering performed).
- Downstream scoring/persistence correctness — untouched by this diff.

## D) Qualified verdict: APPROVE WITH FIXES
The layer is soundly built and genuinely meets all five criteria at the code level: segregation and the auth gate are fail-closed and defense-in-depth, the CSP is honestly strict with htmx correctly kept eval-free, secrets stay in env, and the design-system mapping is faithful. Context cut observed: I read only the diff, the touched source files, the schema/migrations, and the permitted rules/spec/ADR. I did not open the worklog, plans, sessions or the task file.

## A) Per-criterion verdict

**Criterion 1 — Two apps compile clean and serve the themed base layout (Gray 100, local IBM Plex, design-system conformant): MET (with an evidence caveat).**
- `render.lisp` builds both pages; `role-scope`/`role-context` (render.lisp:35-52) differentiate agent vs manager. Dark-theme tokens are embedded in `app.css:690-703` and mirror `.claude/assets/tokens/dark-theme-tokens.css` exactly (`--bg-base:#161616` etc.). Six IBM Plex woff2 faces are vendored and `@font-face`'d locally (`app.css:663-687`), satisfying design.md's local-fonts rule. No `box-shadow`/glow; elevation is by layered bg + hairline borders, per design.md.
- Caveat: the automated suite renders strings and validates them with vnu, but the *served* layout (real Hunchentoot response, static middleware resolving `/assets/*`) is exercised only by the manual `run-web.lisp`. See Finding 1.

**Criterion 2 — HTMX 2.0.x served static under strict CSP with `allowEval:false`: MET.**
- Vendored file is htmx `version:"2.0.4"` (confirmed in `src/web/static/htmx.min.js`). Loaded as same-origin static asset `/assets/htmx.min.js` (render.lisp:65). Config is delivered as a `<meta name="htmx-config">` tag (render.lisp:64, value `+htmx-config+` render.lisp:19-20) with `allowEval:false` — not an inline script, so it survives `script-src 'self'`. CSP (`server.lisp:26-31`) carries no `unsafe-inline`/`unsafe-eval`. Consistent and correct. One latent gap for the next phase — see Finding 3.

**Criterion 3 — Passwordless selection login sets the correct server session per role; apps segregated (no role management): MET at the logic layer; end-to-end unproven.**
- Segregation is enforced twice, fail-closed: (a) the login query is role-scoped by `ecase` selecting `sales_agents` vs `sales_managers` (queries.lisp:15-23, 33-43), so an opposite-role username finds no row and is rejected; (b) the home gate `role-authorized-p` (session.lisp:39-43) requires the session role to `eq` the app's role, so an agent-role session hitting the manager app is redirected to `/login` (handlers.lisp:47-53). `username` is bound as `$1`, never interpolated. Login input is validated and empty/missing/unknown all funnel to the error page (handlers.lisp:33-38). Verified against schema: `username TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` on both tables (`db/migrations/0001_reference.sql:21,28`), so the `:single` lookup is safe.
- Two reservations: the real cookie/session round-trip and ningle POST-param shape are not covered by automated tests (Finding 1), and the two apps share a session-cookie name on a shared host (Finding 2).

**Criterion 4 — Base layout responsive on iPhone 13 (navbar collapse): MET.**
- `@media (max-width:820px)` reveals `.nav-toggle` and hides `.nav-tabs`, restored via the pure-CSS `.nav-cb:checked ~ .nav-tabs` toggle (app.css:862-873); the checkbox precedes `.nav-tabs` as a sibling in `render-navbar` (render.lisp:84-92), so the selector is valid. A second breakpoint at 560px tightens padding. The checkbox carries `aria-label`. 390px falls inside the 820px breakpoint.

**Criterion 5 — Applicable software verification passes: MET (asserted precondition, not re-run).**

## B) Findings (most severe first)

**1 — MEDIUM — automated suite verifies route logic but not the live session/POST round-trip.**
`tests/web/*` drive the `-for` cores with a hand-built `fresh-session` hash-table (session.lisp test:1126) and stub `*lookup-user-fn*`/`*list-usernames-fn*`. This proves the gate/redirect/mutation logic, but three integration points that Criterion 3 actually requires are unexercised: (a) that Lack persists the in-place-mutated session hash-table and emits `Set-Cookie` on the 302 (handlers.lisp:36-38 relies on it); (b) that ningle delivers POST body params as the string-keyed alist `login-submit-for` assumes at `(assoc "user" params :test #'string=)` (handlers.lisp:33) — if ningle's shape differs, login silently always fails to the error page; (c) that the static middleware resolves `/assets/app.css|htmx.min.js|fonts/*`. This is the classic pass-while-checking-something-narrower gap. *Remediation:* make human sign-off contingent on a `run-web.lisp` walk-through — login→home→logout on *both* apps, plus a cross-role attempt — and record the observation; optionally add one Clack integration test that issues a real request against a booted app.

**2 — MEDIUM — both apps use the same session cookie name on a shared host, so they collide on localhost.**
`make-app` installs `(:session :state (make-cookie-state :httponly t :samesite :lax))` (server.lisp:47-49) for both roles; the Lack session middleware defaults the cookie name to `lack.session` for both. Cookies are host-scoped, not port-scoped (RFC 6265 §8.5), so on `127.0.0.1:8081` and `:8082` the two `lack.session` cookies overwrite each other: logging into the agent app, then opening the manager app in the same browser, makes the manager mint a fresh session and `Set-Cookie` over the shared name, silently logging the agent out. No privilege escalation (the role gate is fail-closed), but it breaks using both apps in one browser — precisely the manual verification Criteria 1/3/4 depend on. The code comment at server.lisp:9 ("segregação é por origem: cada porta tem o seu próprio cookie") is factually wrong for a shared host. *Remediation:* give each app a distinct cookie name via the session middleware `:key` option (e.g. `lack.session.agent` / `lack.session.manager`).

**3 — LOW — CSP has no `connect-src`, so `default-src 'none'` will block htmx AJAX the moment it is used.**
`+content-security-policy+` (server.lisp:26-31) omits `connect-src`; htmx XHR/fetch falls back to `default-src 'none'`. This phase ships no `hx-*` AJAX attributes, so Criterion 2 is fully met, but the next phase's first `hx-get` will be blocked. Latent coupling worth recording now. *Remediation:* add `connect-src 'self'` when AJAX is introduced.

**4 — LOW — partial-start leaves an inconsistent handler state.**
In `start` (server.lisp:562-579) the agent is `clackup`'d before the manager; if the manager `clackup` errors, the agent handler stays live with `*agent-handler*` set, and the guard at server.lisp:567 then rejects a retry with "já estão em execução" until `stop` is called. `stop` is correctly idempotent and cleans up, so recovery exists, but the window is untidy. *Remediation:* wrap the second `clackup` so a failure tears down the first.

**5 — LOW — `role-authorized-p`/`authenticated-p` assume a non-nil session table.**
`authenticated-p` (session.lisp:26-28) calls `gethash` on `table` without a nil guard; it is safe today only because both call sites (`home-response-for` handlers.lisp:50, `logout-response-for` handlers.lisp:44) guard `table` first, and the Lack middleware always supplies one. Noted for defense-in-depth; no action required for this phase.

No high-severity findings. Secrets: none hardcoded — `config.lisp` reads only ports/bind/static-root from env with dev defaults and explicitly confines DB credentials to `src/db.lisp`/`PG*` (config.lisp:5-8), satisfying security-by-design. CLOS: only the library class `ningle:app` is instantiated (server.lisp:516); no project-owned `defclass`/`defgeneric`/`defmethod`, per CLAUDE.md. SQL: parameterized, no `SELECT *`, single-table queries so unqualified columns are within std-sql.md. Every function carries a contract docstring.

## C) Deliberately out of audit scope
- The asserted automatic verification (compile-clean, mallet, Parachute 68+102, vnu) — taken as a satisfied precondition, not re-run.
- Binary integrity/subsetting of the six woff2 fonts and the exact byte content of `htmx.min.js` beyond confirming the `2.0.4` version string.
- Visual/pixel fidelity to the `.claude/assets/examples/` prototypes (no rendering performed).
- Downstream scoring/persistence correctness — untouched by this diff.

## D) Qualified verdict: APPROVE WITH FIXES
The layer is soundly built and genuinely meets all five criteria at the code level: segregation and the auth gate are fail-closed and defense-in-depth, the CSP is honestly strict with htmx correctly kept eval-free, secrets stay in env, and the design-system mapping is faithful. The reservations are not correctness defects in the shipped logic but evidence and robustness gaps: Criterion 3's real cookie/session and POST-param round-trip is proven only by manual `run-web.lisp`, not the automated suite (Finding 1), and the shared cookie name (Finding 2) actively degrades that same manual verification on localhost. I recommend the human approve conditional on (a) a recorded `run-web.lisp` walk-through of login/home/logout plus a cross-role attempt on both apps, and (b) the distinct per-app cookie name from Finding 2; Findings 3-5 can be deferred to the backlog.</result>

;;;; integration.lisp --- Teste de integração em processo da pilha web.

(in-package #:leadscorer/web/tests)

;;; Este teste exercita a pilha real de middleware (cabeçalho de segurança,
;;; ativos estáticos e sessão do Lack) e o roteamento Ningle, chamando o app
;;; Clack embrulhado em processo, sem abrir portas nem cliente HTTP. Fecha a
;;; lacuna que os testes de lógica '-for' não cobrem: a persistência da sessão
;;; com Set-Cookie, a forma dos parâmetros POST entregue pelo Ningle e a
;;; resolução dos ativos estáticos. As consultas ao banco são substituídas por
;;; indireções vinculadas, de modo que o teste dispensa PostgreSQL.

(defun make-env (method path &key cookie body)
  "Constrói um ambiente Clack mínimo para METHOD e PATH, com um cabeçalho de
cookie COOKIE opcional e um corpo urlencoded BODY opcional (para POST)."
  (let ((headers (make-hash-table :test 'equal)))
    (when cookie (setf (gethash "cookie" headers) cookie))
    (let ((env (list :request-method method :script-name "" :path-info path
                     :server-name "localhost" :server-port 8081
                     :server-protocol :http/1.1 :request-uri path
                     :url-scheme "http" :remote-addr "127.0.0.1"
                     :query-string "" :headers headers)))
      (when body
        (let ((octets (sb-ext:string-to-octets body :external-format :utf-8)))
          (setf (gethash "content-type" headers) "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
          (setf env (append env
                            (list :content-type "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
                                  :content-length (length octets)
                                  :raw-body (flexi-streams:make-in-memory-input-stream
                                             octets))))))
      env)))

(defun cookie-header-from (response)
  "Extrai o par 'nome=valor' do cabeçalho Set-Cookie de RESPONSE, apto a ser
reenviado como cabeçalho Cookie, ou NIL quando ausente."
  (let ((set-cookie (getf (second response) :set-cookie)))
    (when set-cookie
      (subseq set-cookie 0 (position #\; set-cookie)))))

(defun body-string (response)
  "Decodifica o corpo de RESPONSE em string. Trata o corpo em octetos das
respostas de HTML e a lista de strings de outras respostas."
  (let ((body (third response)))
    (typecase body
      ((vector (unsigned-byte 8)) (sb-ext:octets-to-string body :external-format :utf-8))
      (list (apply #'concatenate 'string (remove-if-not #'stringp body)))
      (string body)
      (t ""))))

(define-test web-stack-round-trip-in-process
  "Percorre login, home autenticada, papel cruzado e logout pela pilha real."
  (let ((leadscorer/web::*lookup-user-fn*
          (lambda (role username)
            (if (and (eq role :agent) (string= username "anna.snelling")) 42 nil)))
        (leadscorer/web::*list-usernames-fn*
          (lambda (role) (declare (ignore role)) *sample-usernames*))
        (agent (leadscorer/web::make-agent-app))
        (manager (leadscorer/web::make-manager-app)))
    ;; 1) A tela de login é servida com o markup e os usuários semeados.
    (let ((r (funcall agent (make-env :get "/login"))))
      (is = 200 (first r))
      (true (search "text/html" (getf (second r) :content-type)))
      (true (search "content-security-policy"
                    (string-downcase (format nil "~{~a ~}" (second r)))))
      (let ((html (body-string r)))
        (true (search "Aplicação do agente" html))
        (true (search "value=anna.snelling" html))))
    ;; 2) O ativo estático é resolvido pela middleware de estáticos.
    (let ((r (funcall agent (make-env :get "/assets/app.css"))))
      (is = 200 (first r))
      (true (search "text/css" (getf (second r) :content-type))))
    ;; 3) A home sem sessão é negada por padrão (fail-closed).
    (let ((r (funcall agent (make-env :get "/"))))
      (is = 302 (first r))
      (is equal "/login" (getf (second r) :location)))
    ;; 4) O login válido grava a sessão e emite o cookie próprio do app.
    (let* ((r (funcall agent (make-env :post "/login" :body "user=anna.snelling")))
           (cookie (cookie-header-from r)))
      (is = 302 (first r))
      (is equal "/" (getf (second r) :location))

A auditoria independente foi conduzida por um agente com contexto deliberadamente cortado, que

## Criterios de aceitacao (resultado)

- (1) Duas apps sobem sem avisos e servem o layout base tematizado: MET. Tokens Gray 100 e seis

- (2) HTMX 2.0.x estatico sob CSP estrita com 'allowEval' falso: MET. htmx 2.0.4 servido de

- (3) Login por selecao estabelece a sessao correta por papel; apps segregados: MET no nivel de

  pura; 390 px cai dentro do breakpoint.
- (5) Verificacao de software aplicavel passa: MET (precondicao).

## Conformidade de design nao capturada pela verificacao automatica

- Estilo funcional; nenhum CLOS proprio (apenas a classe de biblioteca 'ningle:app'). SQL
  parametrizado, sem 'SELECT *', consultas de tabela unica. Segredos so por ambiente; credenciais
